items.text: I woke beneath the mountain with a dead radio and a glyph that hummed under my hand. To understand how I got there, I have to go back three days.
We reached camp under gathering cloud. The survey showed chambers too symmetrical to be natural, and on the eastern ridge I found a sealed Vaelor door.
Water opened the first ruin, and its inscription named the Voice Below. This stone was built to carry sound the way roads carry people.
The bridge gave way, and I fell alone into the fissure. Its anchors hadn't failed. Someone had cut them.
I followed air and water through the dark and got the radio working. Nadiya's warning came too late. Meridian was already below.
I slipped past Lucian Drake's patrols. Their crates proved one thing: someone gave them our route before we ever opened the door.
I drained the drowned temple, and the lower gate rose out of the water. Beyond it was a city no one had seen in centuries.
The City of Echoes left its warning on the walls: the Vault worked, until it didn't. Then Tomas called. The team was waiting.
Elias was hurt, and the Key was gone. Adrian sold our coordinates to Meridian, and now Drake holds the way into the Vault.
Drake's charges tore the Heart Road apart around me. I reached the Vault threshold with the mountain shaking at my back.
I broke the four nodes, and the feedback tore the Vault out of Drake's hands. Then the chamber began to seal, and I ran.
Tomas pulled me onto the ridge as the mountain closed behind us. Everyone made it out. The Vault stays buried.
Mara? Oh, thank God. Listen to me. Meridian contractors are in the valley. Armed.
Meridian. Armed, and standing between me and the water. Stay low.
Nadiya... there's a city down here. An entire city.
They built a city under the mountain. And every stone is still listening.
A tomb sealed with counterweights. They engineered even their grief.
Drake's charges are shaking the conduits loose. The whole mountain feels it.
Hear that, Vale? Every fault line on Earth, waiting for a conductor.
